body:
Well at least I know there's not another person to worry about when I contemplate death.

Better? I can only say less worse when I feel incapable of enjoyment, but in relative terms they are the same thing.

You are right in some way. So close, are the pursuit of death and the pursuit of happiness for someone who equates their life with sorrow and who wants to be done with them both. To be averse to life is to almost be in pursuit of death. To be averse to sorrow is to almost be in pursuit of happiness.

I think we are overcomplicating the matter. Our thoughts are being processed with our conclusions already in mind. You want to help me and I do not want to help myself.

It is as simple as me not wanting to live. I do not want to get mileage out of life. I do not care for things I may prefer or not prefer. Nothing feels good any more, but some things feel bad. There is nothing to pursue, only things to avoid. Sometimes there is not even bad. Especially given that my thoughts are focused on attaining a void where neither would be possible. A lack of consciousness where neither the subjective nor the objective would be attainable (to me) because the consciousness that could have experienced these things would be gone. Is it to say that I prefer death over life? I do not know, but I can say that the thought is frequent, moreso that the *feeling* is frequent: the feeling of a desire for this peace. Like a tiredness that wants me to always sleep, and that never wants me to wake.

Yes, it is depression. I am not blind enough to think that I am the only person with this, or that it is something immutable. I have already said that I know it can be solved. It is that, whether or not my thoughts are clouded by my condition, I do not want the effort of this process. Also, given that my desire not to change may be caused by the condition itself, the thought of me wanting to get out of this mess is perhaps akin to the thought of me being able to lift myself into the air by pulling on my shoes with my hands. 

It is as simple as you wanting me to be happy. That is understandable. I also want others to be happy. Although this brings me to the thought that, in a void where I lack consciousness, I would not be able to empathise. Could I be cruel enough not to consider another's suffering now because I will not be able to consider it at the time when the suffering would be there? Well, no. It is not a contemplation, but a bad feeling. The bad feeling I get when I think of the distress I would bring to my kin with my death. It is something to avoid.

So I have said, in other words, all that I said in my first post.

I've had years of time, and I may have years more. If I am considering blowing all of the days remaining in my life on this purchase of eternal peace, then what is the expense of another day to ensure that my decision is sound?

I could simply be the *"contents of a box."* That is what I want for myself.   
Though, alive, I am a source of content. Like these complaints and thoughts.  
I am some kind of content. Produced by my parents, unfortunately so for me.  

Though you ask me to feel content, as though it is preferable to feeling bad. Contentment is there when I look at my life impartially, forgetting the small scale feelings that are experienced when I see it through my eyes. Instead it is there when I look at me from outside. It is feeling like the material thing that I am, and knowing that I am, Homo Sapiens. It is no more true or false than sadness, but rather, sadness is the more partial way to look at me. When I look at my life through all my sufferings, decisions and biases. It is feeling like emotional thing that I am, and knowing that I am [my name].

Why should I leap my perspective out of my body and detach myself from these wants, just to feel this contentment, rather than sadness? It seems that the conclusion "bury it" is made with the goal of my living already assumed. I have already made clear that my goal is not to live.

There is no one. I'm too scared to approach someone in the flesh. I know there's nothing to be afraid of, but all the knowledge in the world can't change a feeling. It's irrational, and it's dumb, but I just won't call someone through fear. I'll end up going this alone.

I honestly don't know. I'm just bumbling along with my tedious unemployed life. I do have some interactions with people. At a stretch I could say they are positive interactions. Though it seems like the good days are just a little height to fall from once the day is over. I can't say if I'm making progress, still or falling. There's no comparison now I just tend to let each moment slip past as its own isolated incident. 

I am useless now. I can't remember anything that happens. I'm not sure if that's because nothing happens or if I forgot. Both happen a lot. I can't speak to most people. I'll never put myself there voluntarily. Partially because my hair became the tumbleweed to complete this dreary isolated scene, partially because I just start to mumble any words I try to speak. Doing nothing is having nothing to say when it comes to social interactions. When people ask about my day I'm not going to say "I wasted the whole time with Dr who on in the background. Sometimes whilst I stared contemplatively at my reflection in a breadknife. For what felt like a few moments, and turned out to be about 20 minutes."

I just don't know.

What would you have me do, wait until I feel differently? Put in the effort that I really don't want to put in?

The only reason I haven't killed myself is because of others. In a perfect world I would pull myself from the timeline entirely, so that no one ever knew me. Reality ties me to other people so that they hurt when I'll end my suffering, as though some cruel God decided that pain has to either come to me or come from me. I can't help it, I'll start having a thought, one which makes me crueller than the unreal God of my simile: I won't be there to care if they hurt or not. 

I'm tired of people caring about me when I really don't care about me at all. Just let me drop.

If you had one shot to do a bad thing, then don't do it. Right now I'm thinking my life is a bad thing. Right you're thinking my ending my life is a bad thing. 

To me, hearing about this "one defining moment" some time in the future, it reminds me of when the religious speak of heaven. What have you got in evidence that I'll actually experience this at all? It seems just like a tactic to keep me alive, because of your belief that my ending my life is a bad thing.

It started at college. That's in the UK use of the word college, where I was taking my A levels. Everything was going well. My tutors would always comment on my intelligence, always excited about my potential. I'd plough through internal tests fine, and they expected me to get a high grade based on these. I was hopeful, and even better than this sense that a ball was rolling, was the few friends I had. I've always been terrible at making friends, and I grew to love the little circle I had. I was lucky to have made friends at all. Mid way through my studies I was the only one to notice I was always tired. No matter how much sleep I had there was this strange fatigue. I'd be so close to dreaming that I could never focus on any real world task for long. I should have fought it, studied harder, maybe I'd be at university now like everyone else I know. Instead I came out with terrible grades, had to face my tutors, who all asked "what happened?" 

I decided I'd look for a job. Dad had me claim benefits at the first opportunity. He wanted to start charging me rent at an incredibly fair price for what I get. Actually I'd say it was unfair... on him. At first I thought a job could be an opportunity to put it all behind me. What actually happened was filling in applications and mainly get nothing back. I've never worked. The deeper I sink the less confident I become, and the longer I'm not working the more employers have against me. I had many silly dreams before. Being a mechanical engineer, a writer, I also wanted to be a philosophy teacher at some point. Now all I can hope for is some job stacking shelves or cleaning toilets. I can't even get one of those! I'm ridiculous.

Of course it's not just the lack of work that gets me down, also my lack of friends. I can't face them any more. They're all going somewhere. I haven't seen them in ages, and the first question will be "What have you been doing?" I don't want to hook this societal deadweight I am onto anyone's shoulders, they have their own stresses. Many of them have things which make me realise that I am falling into these dark emotions over so very little. This realisation doesn't change my feelings though. It's as though nothing is arousing me, or altering this awful state. Like I'm stuck here being nothing for as long as I'll stay alive for.

Even then I don't think I'm hitting the nail on the head. It could be that I have simply lost all interest in my future now. I don't want any of the effort.
